title: Lyapunov spectrum of random neural networks
abstract: The Lyapunov spectrum of a nonlinear recurrent neural network with random asymmetric couplings is calculated in the limit $N\to\infty$. The calculation is based on a finite-$N$ identity that expresses the cumulative distribution of Lyapunov exponents as a response function of the tangent-space dynamics, with the tangent trajectory selected by a minimum-norm condition rather than by an initial condition. A cavity method then determines this response function at large $N$ through a self-consistent single-site problem. This result establishes that the chaos in this network is extensive and gives access to diffeomorphism-invariant properties of the dynamics. This work was done in collaboration with the AI models GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5.
summary: This theoretical work determines the full Lyapunov spectrum for large random neural networks by mapping the problem onto a response function solvable via a cavity method. It proves that the network exhibits extensive chaos, providing fundamental, diffeomorphism-invariant properties of the dynamics. The methodology bridges concepts from statistical physics (cavity method) and dynamical systems theory (Lyapunov exponents).
main_problem: The paper calculates the full Lyapunov spectrum of a nonlinear recurrent neural network with random asymmetric couplings in the thermodynamic limit ($N	o\infty$).
main_result: The chaos in the network is established to be extensive, meaning key measures like the attractor dimension and entropy rate scale linearly with system size $N$.
method: The calculation employs a cavity method applied to a response function derived from a finite-$N$ identity relating the Lyapunov spectrum to the tangent-space dynamics.
model_or_system: The model is a random neural network (rate network) governed by discrete-time dynamics $x(n+1) = G(x(n))$, with couplings $J_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, g^2/N)$.
key_observables: Lyapunov exponents ($\lambda_i$), Attractor Dimension ($D_{KY}$), Entropy Rate ($h_{KS}$), and the cumulative distribution function $F(s)$ of the exponents.
important_parameters: System size $N$ (limit $N	o\infty$), coupling strength $g$, and time step $\delta$ (limit $\delta	o 0$ for continuous time).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the minimum-norm selection of the tangent trajectory and assumes the exchange of limits ($\lim_{N	o\infty}$ and $\lim_{	ext{regularization}	o 0}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectrum $F(s)$ vs $s$, the Schrödinger problem for the continuous-time limit, and the maximum Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_1$ as a function of coupling strength $g$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by relating the spectrum to a response function. It then uses the cavity method to compute this response function in the large-$N$ limit, culminating in the determination of the spectrum edge $s^*$ via single-site theory.
why_interesting: The rigorous analytical determination of the full spectrum and the confirmation of extensive chaos in a complex, non-linear system provides deep insights into the information processing capacity and dynamical stability of large-scale artificial neural systems.

Figure 2 shows the attractor dimension and the participation ratios (Fig. 2a) and the entropy rate (Fig. 2b) as functions of g for several time steps δ. The theory and the simulations again agree closely. At every time step, the two participation ratios and the entropy rate increase monotonically with g over the range of g shown, and the participation ratios grow more slowly at strong coupling, as also found numerically by Engelken et al. [22]. The attractor dimension saturates at strong coupling and, as found numerically [22], eventually decreases. Over the range of g shown, this decrease is visible at δ = 0.5, where the attractor dimension has a maximum near g = 10.
